lines.text: Do you know how your eyes see colour? There's no colour in light itself, only waves of different lengths.
The light we can see runs from about four hundred nanometers, violet, to about seven hundred, red.
At the back of your eye, millions of cone cells catch it. There are three kinds, most sensitive to red, green, and blue light.
Every colour you see is just a mix of how strongly those three fire. Red and green cones firing together? Your brain says yellow.
That's why screens only need red, green, and blue pixels. Mix them, and they trick your cones into seeing millions of colours.
If one type of cone is missing or shifted, some colours look the same. That's colour blindness, in about one in twelve men.
Many birds have a fourth kind of cone, for ultraviolet light we can't see at all.
So colour isn't really out there. It's made inside your head.
